title: Life Dashboard Companion for Android: Health Connect export
description: Life Dashboard Companion for Android exports Health Connect data and screen time per app to Home Assistant, MQTT or your own webhook. Open source, no cloud.
h1: Health Connect and screen time, sent to your own server
lead: Life Dashboard Companion is an open-source Android app that sends Health Connect data and screen time per app to Home Assistant, MQTT or your own webhook, with no cloud and no account. It reads what Samsung Health, Google Health, Garmin Connect, Oura, Withings and others write to Health Connect.

highlights.title: 33 Health Connect types
highlights.text: Steps, sleep stages, heart rate, HRV, weight, blood pressure, glucose, workouts, nutrition and cycle tracking, each with its own switch.

highlights.title: Every record, with its source
highlights.text: Each record goes out with a stable ID and the app that wrote it. Daily totals count a walk once.

highlights.title: All your history
highlights.text: Backfill from 30 days up to 5 years, or everything Health Connect has. In Home Assistant each day lands on its own date in long-term statistics, for now about the last year.

highlights.title: Screen time per app
highlights.text: Foreground minutes for every app, with a day boundary you choose and a filter that keeps the apps you pick out of what's sent.

highlights.title: Three ways out
highlights.text: The Life Dashboard integration, MQTT with Home Assistant Discovery, or any webhook that accepts a JSON POST. Several at once works too.

highlights.title: Receive into Health Connect
highlights.text: Scale and blood pressure readings from Home Assistant go into Health Connect, where Samsung Health and Google Health read weight.

sections.h2: Into Home Assistant, with or without a broker
sections.text: The Life Dashboard integration pairs with one QR code and keeps every day in long-term statistics. MQTT with Home Assistant Discovery suits a setup that already runs a broker and only needs current values.

bullets.sub: Today's steps, distance and calories, the latest heart rate, sleep, weight, blood pressure, glucose and more, and the last workout. MQTT gets 24, without the workout.

bullets.main: Screen time in total and per app
bullets.sub: Both routes get the totals. The sensor per app comes with the integration.
Give each a Phone name under Advanced, and each gets its own device and topics.

sections.h2: Every record as JSON, to a server you run
sections.text: Point the app at n8n, Node-RED, the Grafana stack or a short script. A webhook also gets what no sensor holds: single meals, cycle tracking entries and workout details.

bullets.sub: An X-Signature header your server can check. Generate creates a secret of 32 random bytes.
Picked from Android's credential store, for a server behind a reverse proxy that requires one.
Up to 700 payloads wait while your server is down, and the next sync sends them first.
A record deleted in Health Connect is named in the next payload, so your receiver can drop it too.

sections.h2: Android screen time per app, next to your health data
sections.text: The app reads foreground time per app from Android's usage statistics, the same numbers Digital Wellbeing uses. Screen time has its own schedule and webhooks, and works without Health Connect on Android 8.0 or newer.

bullets.main: A day boundary of your own
bullets.sub: On by default at 04:00, so phone use after midnight counts toward the day before.
An app you filter out is not named in what's sent; the day's total still counts its time.

bullets.main: The last 7 days in every sync
bullets.sub: A day that was still running at one sync is corrected by the next.

bullets.main: A sensor per app in Home Assistant
bullets.sub: Created disabled, so you enable only the apps you want to automate on.

requirements: Health data needs Android 9 or newer with Health Connect, which is built into Android 14 and later and comes from Google Play on Android 9 through 13. Screen time works on Android 8.0 and newer. The Life Dashboard integration needs Home Assistant 2026.3 or newer with HACS. MQTT needs a broker, and a webhook needs a server that accepts a JSON POST.

faq.q: Which Health Connect types become Home Assistant sensors?
faq.a: 25 of the 33 through the integration, 24 over MQTT. The other eight (nutrition, mindfulness, sexual activity and five cycle tracking types) are events rather than values, so they get no sensor; the integration counts mindfulness minutes per day. Workouts get a last workout sensor and the minutes of today and yesterday in the integration. A webhook of your own gets those records in full.

faq.q: Can it send to Home Assistant and a webhook at the same time?
faq.a: Yes. Every address has its own signing secret and headers, and pairing with Home Assistant sets them only for the address it adds, so a second receiver keeps its own. One thing to know today: a payload counts as delivered once one destination takes it, so a destination that's down at that moment misses it. Health Connect and Screen Time can each send to several webhooks and to MQTT at once. A delivery of its own for every destination is planned.

faq.q: What happens when my server is down?
faq.a: Each sync writes its payload to the phone first and deletes it only once a webhook has accepted it. The outbox holds up to 700 Health Connect payloads, about a week of syncs at the 15-minute interval, and the next sync that gets through delivers them first.

faq.q: Can it sync at fixed times instead of an interval?
faq.a: Yes. Each tab has its own Sync Schedule: every 15 minutes or longer, or a list of times, on the days you pick, with quiet hours. A Quick Settings tile, Tasker and MacroDroid can start a sync too.

No. Readings come back in the integration's signed response to the webhook call the app already makes, so Receive needs the Life Dashboard integration. Smart scale to Samsung Health walks through the setup.

faq.q: How does the app store my secrets?
faq.a: Auth headers, signing secrets and MQTT passwords are encrypted with AES-256-GCM, with a key the Android Keystore holds. Android's own backup leaves them out, along with the webhook logs.

faq.q: How much battery does it use?
faq.a: Between syncs the app does nothing: no service keeps running and no connection stays open. Each sync is a short job that Android starts on your schedule. On Samsung, Xiaomi and similar phones, set the app's battery usage to Unrestricted, or Android stops the scheduled syncs; the setup guide has the paths per brand.

faq.q: What does the app ask for, and what leaves the phone?
faq.a: Health Connect read permissions for the types you switch on, write permissions only for the Receive types you switch on, usage access for screen time, the camera only while you scan a pairing code, internet access, and notifications for failed syncs and backfill progress. Data goes only to the addresses you enter. The privacy policy lists every permission and every field.

Yes: Life Dashboard Companion on Google Play, €4.99 once (US$4.99), with no subscription. It's the easy way, with automatic updates, and buying it supports development. The APK on GitHub, Obtainium and F-Droid stay free: the same app, built from the same source and signed with the same key.

faq.q: Can I switch between GitHub, Obtainium, F-Droid and Google Play later?
faq.a: Yes. Google Play, the APK on GitHub, Obtainium and F-Droid all install the same app, with the same package name and the same signing key, so you can switch without reinstalling: one installs over the other and your settings stay.
